PROJECT BRIEF · 5 NOVEMBER 2026

Trading. Agent wallets.
One shared gas vision.

MateX combines trading, research and AI agent wallets with MATEx GAS: a single-token gas and payment layer being built across supported blockchains. The proposed Circle grant work connects this product to Arc USDC settlement, useful agent services and a bounded sponsorship pilot.

Website source on GitHub ↗Developer status and docs ↗

Product demo and transcript

A 100-second walkthrough starts with fragmented network gas, then covers the smart-contract design, wallet and MCP agent flow, an internal Arc testnet conversion, and historical trading research. The transcript names the Circle products used and their codebase locations.

Watch the demo ↗Read transcript ↗Demo files in Drive ↗

1. The problem

Users and AI agents operating across blockchains must manage different native gas tokens, funding steps and payment rules. Trading workflows add research, execution costs and transaction checks. This fragmentation makes it harder to operate agent wallets with a clear spending budget and a reliable view of what settled.

MATEx GAS aims to let users and agents fund one shared gas-token account while sponsors pay each supported chain’s native fees. MateX connects that account to trading research and agent tools. Every paid action should have a bounded quote, explicit authority and a matching receipt.

2. Why Arc and USDC

Arc is the intended settlement backbone for the proposed grant phase: useful services paid in USDC, a future USDC funding route for agent gas, and verifiable settlement behind MGAS accounting. x402 provides a payment interaction for paid resources, while MCP connects agent tools and structured receipts. The shared-gas funding route and bridging remain roadmap work. A separate internal Arc testnet converter has demonstrated 1 test USDC purchasing 100 tMGAS; it is separate from x402 checkout and Base service credits.

The current Arc testnet adapter uses Circle’s hosted Facilitator Service for exact USDC checkout. A fixed account snapshot is priced at 0.011 test USDC: 0.010 resource price plus a 0.001 service markup. The buyer signs an exact payment authorization; the seller separately signs its settlement proof in the present prototype.

Current implementation is documented against Circle’s Facilitator Service quickstart. A live owner-signed Arc settlement receipt is still an outstanding validation step. No commercial partnership or grant award is claimed.

3. What is built

Arc testnet converter

An internal owner-operated purchase exchanged 1 test USDC for 100 tMGAS at the fixed 100:1 rate. Total supply is 10,000 tMGAS and remaining inventory is 9,900. Inspect the purchase receipt ↗. This is test evidence, not external adoption.

Arc checkout adapter

Local testnet requests, bounded prices, explicit buyer and seller wallet approvals, settlement verification, recovery of uncertain states and MCP receipt retrieval.

Connected trading research

MateX’s actual fee-aware historical backtests and transaction reconciliation reports are available through the shared-credit preview. It reserves funds once, settles on delivery and returns reservations on failure.

Agent Control Center

Owner-signed policies enforce per-request, daily and weekly USDC service budgets, allowed reports, report networks, recipients and expiry. Pause and connection-key rotation also need owner review. The scope is the new managed Arc-report connector; existing manual and legacy flows remain separate.

Managed Arc report delivery

Frozen-input backtests and transaction checks are linked to exact Arc USDC settlement, a budget reservation and matching payment/delivery receipts. A separate authenticated four-tool local MCP entry returns the original report and evidence. Canonical payment checks use cryptographic fixtures; a live user-wallet policy and report purchase remain to be demonstrated.

Base-funded shared account

One canonical Base tMGAS deposit creates one prepaid service credit. The operator’s treasury controls tokens; a local SQLite ledger records available, reserved and spent credits.

15-tool MCP preview

A local stdio preview adds owner-reviewed Arc token-purchase requests and receipt retrieval. The user’s MCP client supplies the model. The connector itself needs no model-provider key and cannot sign or submit wallet transactions.

Three project agent skills

A local registry documents Arc tMGAS purchases, the separate Arc account-snapshot checkout and public network inspection. This is a project-owned preview, not an official global skill listing.

Optional local copilot

The separate OpenAI-powered local chat has Arc and read-only Solana modes, with three tools per mode: six capabilities, separate from the 15-tool MCP preview. The provider connection and Solana balance/setup checks have been verified through the browser. Its provider credentials stay in local setup; human wallet review remains required.

Base and Ethereum Sepolia token-paid execution have been demonstrated in earlier flows. These results do not establish Arc settlement, public hosted payments, or a common on-chain token balance across networks.

A MetaMask Solana wallet connection and read-only copilot checks are verified. Devnet RPC identity is checked before operator setup, and the local page displays network connectivity separately from wallet and sponsor readiness. Solana mode uses the selected public Solana address, not the Arc EVM buyer. The current local setup has no configured SPL mint or sponsor. Sponsored execution awaits configuration, funding and transaction evidence. See the developer feature status and connection guide for the current boundaries.

US/USD funding preview

A local Funding hub now includes an installed Circle Onramp Kit 1.0.8 sandbox integration and a separate external handoff to official Arc Portal for real-money USDC purchases. The sandbox uses a wallet-ownership proof and a separate server-only credential. Live provider-session and deposit proof remain pending; existing MATEx payment workflows stay on testnet.

Providers independently determine eligible US states, methods, identity and business onboarding; provider fees are separate from MATEx service markup. Direct Arc off-ramp is unverified. A separately owner-reviewed Arc-to-Base USDC bridge and eligible Coinbase USD checkout are planned, not implemented. No cash-out or MGAS redemption is enabled. Read the funding scope, sandbox limits and official integration sources ↗.

4. Current utility and pricing

The local shared-credit service preview charges 0.055 MGAS credits for a fee and slippage backtest report (0.050 base + 0.005 markup) and 0.011 MGAS credits for payment reconciliation (0.010 base + 0.001 markup). Both are read-only and add zero chain gas. Funding gas is reviewed separately.

The separate managed Arc preview implements the same report services at 0.055 test USDC for a backtest (0.050 + 0.005 markup) and 0.011 for a transaction check (0.010 + 0.001). Its budgets cover USDC service prices and exclude native fees. Buyer and seller wallet approvals remain required. A paid delivery failure keeps the charge and allows the same job to retry delivery without another purchase; it does not trigger an automatic refund. Live wallet proof remains pending. The proposed next phase develops a bounded MGAS gas-sponsorship pilot for agent wallets. MGAS is intended for gas and service fees; trading capital and collateral remain separate. The current Arc checkout does not spend MGAS or automatically convert USDC into it. No bridge, dollar peg or cash redemption promise is implied. Test credits have no cash value.

5. Proposed milestones

  1. Public, reproducible Arc proof: complete testnet USDC/x402 purchases, publish matching transaction evidence and demonstrate result delivery through MCP.
  2. Trading utility and agent wallets: validate the implemented managed Arc report and owner-policy workflow with live wallet approvals, matching payment/delivery receipts and stable request IDs. Retrying a paid delivery must not trigger another payment.
  3. One-balance gas sponsorship pilot: configure and fund a limited network sponsor, reserve an owner-reviewed MGAS fee, verify native gas payment, reconcile actual cost plus markup, and add tenant access, backups, refunds and independent security review.
  4. Developer pilot: validate integrations with external teams and publish completed purchases, failures, repeat use and developer feedback before a production rollout decision.

These are proposed project milestones, not Circle-approved deliverables. Budget, timing, eligibility and acceptance criteria must be finalised through the application and review process.

6. Adoption and ecosystem contribution

The initial audience is developers building trading and other onchain agents that need simpler gas funding, paid research and payment-checking tools. The practical path is a reproducible integration, useful reports, clear approval prompts and receipts that other agent clients can consume. Pilot measurements should include successful delivery, failed delivery, duplicate-charge prevention, integration effort and repeat usage.

This site’s GitHub repository makes the project narrative inspectable. It contains the website and brief, not the private platform implementation. The separately prepared connector has an MIT license; npm and official MCP Registry publication remain pending. There are no claimed customers, pilot partners or adoption numbers yet.

7. Remaining gates

The project is a local testnet developer preview. Shared-credit native gas dispatch remains disabled across Base Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia, BNB Testnet, Arc Testnet and Solana Devnet. Mainnet payments, public hosted execution and unattended spending are not enabled by this website.

Before real funds: review custody and refund terms, protect the hosted service and ledger, fund and verify each native sponsor, reconcile actual settlement costs, complete an independent security review and validate demand through a bounded pilot.
